options: Provides for the right to freedom of religion
Deals with the abolition of the untouchability
explanation: Article 18 abolishes the titles and it permits the military and the academic distinctions, and the National awards were held to be the titles until the 18th Amendment of 1997.

options: to be the titles until the 18th Amendment of 1997
explanation: The Supreme Court held in the 1995 case that the Bharat Ratna, the Padma awards and the other national honours were the titles, and the 18th Amendment of 1997 excluded the awards from Article 18.

options: Deals with the right to education
Prohibits the trafficking in the human beings
explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form, and it is the only article that has been amended.
The Article 16(3), enabling the special provisions for the women, was inserted by the 42nd Amendment of 1976 and the 93rd Amendment of 2005 added the Article 16(4A) for the EWS.

options: Deals with the organisation of the panchayats
Deals with the protection of the environment
Directs the state to promote the educational and the economic interests of the weaker sections
Deals with the equal justice and the free legal aid
explanation: Article 46 directs the state to promote the educational and the economic interests of the weaker sections, the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and other disadvantaged groups.

options: Deals with the protection of the monuments
Directs the state to secure a distribution of the ownership of the material resources in the interest of the people
Deals with the free legal aid
explanation: Article 39(b) directs the state to secure a distribution of the ownership of the material resources of the community in the interest of the people.

q: In the context of the Article 43, which of the following is correct?
options: Was amended by the 42nd Amendment to add the cottage industries in the rural areas
It deals with the free and compulsory education
It deals with the uniform civil code
explanation: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 added the promotion of the cottage industries in the rural areas to the Article 43.

q: In the context of the Article 48, which of the following is correct?
options: Directs the state to organise the agriculture and the animal husbandry on the modern lines
explanation: The Article 48 directs the state to organise the agriculture and the animal husbandry on the modern lines and the prohibition of the slaughter of the cows was added by the 42nd Amendment.

options: Directs the state to secure the right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases
explanation: Article 41 directs the state to secure the right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases and the right to a living wage and the right to the public assistance in the 42nd Amendment.

options: Deals with the free legal aid
Directs the state to provide for the maternity relief
explanation: Article 42, added by the 42nd Amendment, directs the state to provide for the maternity relief and it was a significant advance for the women workers.

options: for the free and compulsory education of the children up to the age of 14
explanation: The original Article 45 directed the state to provide for the free and compulsory education of the children up to the age of 14 and the 86th Amendment of 2002 replaced it with the early childhood care.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Article 47?
options: It deals with the uniform civil code
Directs the state to raise the level of nutrition and improve the standard of living
It deals with the free education
explanation: The Article 47, amended by the 42nd Amendment, directs the state to raise the level of nutrition and improve the standard of living and to promote the public health.
The Article 21A, providing for the free and compulsory education of the children of the age of six to fourteen, was inserted by the 86th Amendment of 2002.

q: The 'right to education' in India became a fundamental right in:
explanation: The right to education became a fundamental right with the 86th Amendment of 2002 and the RTE Act of 2009 gave it the operational shape from 1 April 2010.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The 21 fundamental duties is correct?
options: The 29 subjects of the Union List
explanation: The Eleventh Schedule, added by the 42nd Amendment of 1976, lists the twenty-one fundamental duties of the citizen.

options: The President is the head of the legislature
The President of India is the head of the Union executive
The Prime Minister is the head of the State
The President is the head of the judiciary
explanation: The Article 52 provides that the executive of the Union shall be exercised by the President and it vests the supreme command of the defence forces in him.

options: The President is elected by the electoral college
The President is the head of the Union executive
The President's oath is in the Third Schedule
The term of the President is five years
explanation: The Article 53 provides that the term of the President shall be five years from the date on which he enters into office and the Article 62 provides the same.

options: Provides that the Council of Ministers shall aid and advise the President who shall act in accordance with that advice
It is about the oath of the ministers
It is about the impeachment of the President
It is about the qualifications of the President
explanation: The Article 74(2) makes the advice of the Council of Ministers binding on the President, except in the cases specified in Article 163, and the 42nd and the 44th Amendments modified it.

options: It is about the Union government
Provides that the Council of Ministers shall aid and advise the Governor who shall act in accordance with that advice
explanation: The Article 163 provides that the Council of Ministers shall aid and advise the Governor and the Governor shall act in accordance with that advice, except as specified.

options: It is about the Public Account
The expenditure of the state is subject to the proviso of Article 256 and the annual statement of the estimates
It deals with the revenue expenditure
It is about the Consolidated Fund
explanation: The Article 200 provides that the expenditure of the state shall be subject to the provisions of the proviso to Article 256 and the annual statement of the estimates and it is presented before the legislature.

q: The 'Article 280' of the Constitution deals with:
explanation: The Article 280 provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission by the President every fifth year or earlier if necessary.

q: The 'Article 263' of the Constitution deals with:
explanation: The Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council to inquire into and advise upon the disputes between the states and the subjects of the common interest.

q: The 'Article 262' of the Constitution deals with:
options: The adjudication of the inter-state water disputes
explanation: The Article 262 provides for the adjudication of the disputes relating to the waters of the inter-state rivers and for the creation of the tribunals for that purpose.

q: The 'Article 269' of the Constitution deals with:
options: The taxes levied by the states
The taxes levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the states
explanation: The Article 269 provides for the taxes levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the states and the Article 269A for the inter-state trade of the goods and the services.

q: The 'Article 268' of the Constitution deals with:
options: The taxes levied by the Union but assigned to the states
The taxes levied by the states
explanation: The Article 268 provides for the taxes levied by the Union but assigned to the states and the stamp duties are the important ones under it.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Article 356 is correct?
options: The emergency proclamation of the national emergency
The S.R. Bommai guidelines of the floor test and the judicial review of the proclamation
explanation: In the S.R. Bommai case the Supreme Court laid down the guidelines for the floor test and the judicial review of the proclamation of the President's Rule.

q: The 'National Emergency' under the Article 352 requires the approval of:
options: A two-thirds majority of the Lok Sabha
Both the houses of the Parliament by a special majority
A simple majority of the Lok Sabha
explanation: The proclamation of the national emergency must be approved by both the houses of the Parliament by a special majority and it can be revoked at any time by a simple majority.

q: The 'Article 360' of the Constitution provides for the financial emergency and it has never been:
explanation: The financial emergency under the Article 360 has never been invoked in India and it is a much-restrained power than the national emergency.

options: Allows the suspension of the right to move the courts for the enforcement of the specified fundamental rights during a national emergency
Allows the suspension of all the fundamental rights
explanation: The Article 359 allows the President to suspend the right to move the courts for the enforcement of the specified fundamental rights during a national emergency and the 44th Amendment limited the scope.

options: Provides that the governance of a state under the President's Rule vests in the President
explanation: The Article 365 provides that whenever a state is under the President's Rule, the governance of the state shall vest in the President.

options: Defines the terms of the Government of India and the State and the public servant
Deals with the election of the President
explanation: The Article 366 defines the expressions of the Government of India, the State, the public servant and the legal authority and it was amended by the 42nd Amendment.

options: Added the Articles 48A, 51A and the Tenth Schedule and the 14th, 15th, 16th, 17th and 18th Schedules
It created the Tenth Schedule only
explanation: The 42nd Amendment added the Articles 47A, 48A and 51A and the Tenth Schedule and it was the most sweeping amendment until the 44th.

options: It removed the right to property
Restored the power of the Parliament and the states in the Eighth Schedule of the Official Languages Act
explanation: The 43rd Amendment of 1978 restored the power of the Parliament and the states in the Eighth Schedule of the Official Languages Act and it was done by the Janata government.

options: Inserted the Article 21A for the right to education
explanation: The 86th Amendment of 2002 inserted the Article 21A for the free and compulsory education of the children of the age of six to fourteen and it also changed the Article 45.

options: Froze the allocation of the seats in the Lok Sabha and the assemblies until the census of 2026
explanation: The 91st Amendment of 2003 read down the 84th Amendment and froze the allocation of the seats until the first census after 2026, and it was challenged in the 2008 case that was struck down in 2020.

options: Gave the constitutional status to the cooperative societies
explanation: The 97th Amendment of 2011 gave the constitutional status to the cooperative societies and created the Part IXB in the Constitution.

options: Provided for the 10 per cent reservation for the EWS
explanation: The 103rd Amendment of 2019 provided for the 10 per cent reservation for the economically weaker sections beyond the existing 49.5 per cent and the 77th and the 81st Amendments were also challenged.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the May examine the annual plan is correct?
options: It approves the master plan of the district
May examine the annual plan and the budget of the Gram Panchayat and the elected members of the ward
explanation: The Gram Sabha may examine the annual plan and the prepared budget of the Panchayat and the elected members of the ward and it may make the recommendations on the allocation of the funds.

q: The 'Article 243F' of the Constitution deals with:
explanation: The Article 243F provides for the composition of the Panchayats consisting of the Panch, the members of the ward and the Sarpanch elected directly by the people.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the Article 243G?
options: Lists the powers and the responsibilities of the Panchayats
Deals with the State Election Commission
explanation: The Article 243G lists the powers and the responsibilities of the Panchayats and the Article 243H does the same for the municipalities.

options: Deals with the composition of the Panchayats
Deals with the State Election Commission
Lists the powers and the responsibilities of the municipalities
explanation: The Article 243H lists the powers and the responsibilities of the municipalities and it mirrors the Article 243G of the Panchayats.

options: Provides for the State Election Commission
Provides for the District Planning Committee
explanation: The Article 243ZD provides for a District Planning Committee in every district to consolidate the plans of the Panchayats and the municipalities.

options: Provides for the District Planning Committee
explanation: The Article 243ZE provides for the constitution of the Metropolitan Committees in the metropolitan areas and the Article 243ZC for the metropolitan districts.

options: into force in 1992 with the three-year term
into force on 24 April 1993 with the Panchayats having a five-year term
explanation: The 73rd and the 74th Amendments came into force on 24 April 1993 and they gave the Panchayats and the municipalities a fixed five-year term and the constitutional status.

options: Consists of the elected members of the municipality and of the wards within its jurisdiction
Consists of the officials of the district administration
Consists of the nominees of the state government
Is optional for the municipalities with fewer than three wards
explanation: The 74th Amendment makes the constitution of the Ward Committees compulsory for every municipality with more than three wards and they consist of the elected members of the municipality and of the ward.

q: The 'municipal corporations' are the local bodies for the areas with a population of:
explanation: A municipal corporation is constituted for the areas with a population of one lakh and above, and the 74th Amendment raised the threshold of the metropolitan areas to ten lakh.

q: the NITI Aayog is correct is:
options: It is chaired by the President
Is chaired by the Prime Minister and it has the three-tier structure
explanation: The NITI Aayog, which replaced the Planning Commission in 2015, is chaired by the Prime Minister and it has the three-tier structure and it does not allocate the funds.

q: Is appointed by the President and can be:
options: removed only like a Supreme Court judge
a statutory body of the CAG Act of 1971 only
the auditor of the states only
explanation: The CAG is a constitutional body under the Article 148, is appointed by the President and can be removed only in the manner of a Supreme Court judge.

options: Its members hold office for five years
Is a constitutional body and its chairman and the members hold office for six years
explanation: The UPSC is a constitutional body under the Article 315 and its chairman and the members hold office for six years or up to the age of 65.

options: Lists the specific functions of the UPSC
Provides for the composition of the UPSC
explanation: The Article 320 lists the specific functions of the Public Service Commissions and the Article 315 provides for their constitution.

options: Provides for the tenure of the Election Commissioners
explanation: The Article 316 provides for the tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners and the Article 317 for their removal.

q: The CEC and the ECs are appointed by the President and they can be:
options: removed only like a Supreme Court judge after the 2023 law
explanation: After the 2023 amendment the CEC has the status of a Supreme Court judge and the other commissioners are removable on the CEC's recommendation.

options: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
The National Commission for Women Act, 1990
The National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993
The National Human Rights Commission Act, 1993
explanation: The National Commission for Women was set up in 1990 under the NCW Act of 1990 and it was the outcome of the recommendations of the Committee on the Status of Women in India.

q: The 'NCBC' has the powers of the:
options: Civil court for the matters of the discrimination
explanation: The National Commission for Backward Classes has the powers of a civil court in the matters of the discrimination and the 1993 Act gave it that status.

options: Only the violations in the armed forces
The violations of the human rights within one year of the occurrence
explanation: The NHRC can inquire into the violations of the human rights that have occurred within one year of the occurrence and it can also take up the cases of the armed forces.

q: The 'CVC Act' of 2003 gave the CVC:
explanation: The Central Vigilance Commission (DPC) Act of 2003 gave the statutory status to the CVC, its establishment and the general superintendence of the Government servants.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the Article 148?
options: The CAG is a constitutional body and the CVC and the UPSC are the statutory bodies
explanation: Only the CAG is a constitutional body under the Article 148 and the UPSC and the CVC are the statutory bodies.

q: The Lokpal and the Lokayuktas Act of 2013 gave:
options: the statutory basis to the two ombudsmen
explanation: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act of 2013 gave the statutory basis to the Lokpal and the Lokayuktas, which had existed only as the executive bodies.
The Right to Information Act was passed in 2005 and it came into force on 21 October 2005 with the Central Information Commission in 2005.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Section 8(1)?
options: Gives the citizens the right to the information from the public authorities
Deals with the disqualification of the members of the legislature
explanation: The Section 8(1) of the RTI Act gives the citizens the right to the information from the public authorities and the Section 8(3) for the life and the liberty of the information.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the CIC?
options: Was constituted in 2005 and the first information commissioner was the S.P. Gupta
explanation: The Central Information Commission was constituted in 2005 and the first Chief Information Commissioner was the S. P. Gupta.

q: In the context of the Article 19(1)(a), which of the following is correct?
options: Guarantees the freedom of speech and expression subject to the reasonable restrictions
It applies only to the press
explanation: The freedom of speech and expression under the Article 19(1)(a) is subject to the reasonable restrictions of the Article 19(2) and the Supreme Court has read it expansively in the media and the art cases.

q: The freedom of the press have:
options: The Article 19(2) does not apply to the press
a part of the freedom of speech and expression and the restrictions are the reasonable ones
an absolute right under the Article 19(1)(a)
explanation: The freedom of the press is a part of the freedom of speech and expression under the Article 19(1)(a) and it is subject only to the reasonable restrictions of the Article 19(2).

q: The 'Article 19(2)' of the Constitution lists eight reasonable restrictions, of which:
options: All relate to the morality and the decency
All relate to the contempt of the court and the the the
None of the restrictions are on the speech
Four relate to the sovereignty and the integrity of India, the friendly relations with the foreign states and the public order and the incitement to an offence
explanation: Of the eight restrictions in the Article 19(2), four relate to the sovereignty and the integrity of India, the friendly relations with the foreign states, the public order and the incitement to an offence and the rest to the contempt of the court, the defamation, the morality and the decency and the incitement to a religious offence.

options: Prohibits the ex-post facto criminal laws
explanation: The Article 20(1) says that no person shall be convicted of an offence in respect of any act or omission which was not in force at the time when the act or omission was committed.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Article 20(2) is correct?
explanation: The Article 20(2) says that no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once, and the narrower interpretation was given in the Sajjan Singh case.
The Article 20(3) says that no person accused of an offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.

q: Protects the life and the personal liberty and it has been:
options: read expansively by the Supreme Court
explanation: The Article 21, the right to life and the personal liberty, has been read expansively by the Supreme Court to include the privacy, the clean environment, the livelihood, the health, the shelter and the speedy trial.

q: In the context of the Article 14, which of the following is correct?
options: The equality before the law and the equal protection of the laws
explanation: The Article 14 guarantees the equality before the law and the equal protection of the laws and the judicial review of the differential treatment is possible.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the Article 15?
options: Prohibits the discrimination on the grounds of the religion, the race, the caste, the sex or the place of birth and it permits the special provisions for the socially backward
It applies only to the private citizens
explanation: The Article 15 prohibits the discrimination on the specified grounds and it permits the special provisions for the women, the children and the socially and the educationally backward classes.

options: The reservation for the socially and the educationally backward classes
The reservation for the women only
explanation: The Article 15(4) permits the reservation for the socially and the educationally backward classes and the Article 15(5) for the admission of the SC and the ST in the private institutions.

options: The reservation in the appointments for the backward classes not adequately represented
explanation: The Article 16(4) permits the reservation in the appointments for the backward classes that are not adequately represented in the services of the Union and the states.

options: Deals with the freedom of the religion
Protects the interests of the minorities and the cultural and the educational rights
explanation: The Article 29 protects the interests of the minorities and the Article 30 guarantees the right of the minorities to establish the educational institutions of their choice.

options: Guarantees the right of the minorities to establish and administer the educational institutions of their choice
Deals with the right to the property
Deals with the freedom of the religion
explanation: The Article 30(1) guarantees to all the minorities, whether religious or linguistic, the right to establish and administer the educational institutions of their choice.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Prohibits traffic is correct?
options: Prohibits the traffic in the human beings and the forced labour
explanation: The Article 23 prohibits the traffic in the human beings and the begar and the forced labour and the 103rd Amendment took the manual scavenging out of its ambit.

options: Deals with the freedom of the speech
Guarantees the freedom of conscience and the religion
explanation: The Article 25(1) guarantees the freedom of conscience and the religion and it is subject to the public order, the morality, the health and the other provisions of the Part III.

options: Guarantees the freedom to manage the religious affairs of the religious communities
Deals with the freedom of the speech
explanation: The Article 26 guarantees the freedom to manage the religious affairs of the religious denominations in the matters of religion, the worship and the maintenance of the institutions.

options: Guarantees the freedom of the religion and the worship
explanation: The Article 27 guarantees the freedom of the religion and the worship and it was inserted by the 42nd Amendment.

options: Guarantees the freedom of the religion and the worship and the freedom to profess and practise the religion
explanation: The Article 28, added by the 42nd Amendment, guarantees the freedom of the religion and the worship and the freedom to profess and practise the religion.

options: Guarantees the freedom to form the associations or the unions
explanation: The Article 19(1)(c) guarantees the freedom of the association and the Article 19(1)(f) the freedom of the movement.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the Article 32?
options: It is the right to the information
It is the right to the petition
It is the right to the enforcement of the fundamental rights by the Supreme Court
It is the right to the writs in the High Court
explanation: The Article 32 is the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of the fundamental rights and the Article 226 is the corresponding right before the High Courts.

q: In the context of the Article 226, which of the following is correct?
options: It is about the finance commission
Empowers the High Courts to issue the writs for the enforcement of the fundamental rights and for any other purpose
It is the same as the Article 32
explanation: The Article 226 empowers the High Courts to issue the directions or the orders or the writs for the enforcement of the fundamental rights and for any other purpose, which is wider than the Article 32.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The special leave to appeal is correct?
options: The special leave to appeal to the Supreme Court from any court or tribunal in India
The appellate jurisdiction in the criminal cases
explanation: The Article 136 empowers the Supreme Court to grant the special leave to appeal from the judgment of any court or tribunal in India and it is an extraordinary discretionary power.

options: Makes the law declared by the Supreme Court binding on all the courts in India
explanation: The Article 141 provides that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all the courts within the territory of India.

options: The President may act on his own discretion
The President appoints the Council of Ministers
The President is bound by the judiciary
The President shall act in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers
explanation: The Article 144 binds the President to the advice of the Council of Ministers, except in the cases specified in the Article 163.

options: Empowers the High Court to supervise all the courts and the tribunals in its jurisdiction
Empowers the Supreme Court to supervise the High Courts
Empowers the President to appoint the judges
Empowers the CAG to audit the courts
explanation: The Article 227 empowers the High Court to supervise all the courts and the tribunals in its jurisdiction and to issue the directions to them.

options: Gives the CAG the audit of the courts
Gives the High Court the control of the district and the subordinate courts
Gives the Supreme Court the control of the High Courts
Gives the President the power to appoint the judges
explanation: The Article 235 gives the High Court the control of the district and the subordinate courts in its jurisdiction.

options: Provides for the appointment of the High Court judges
Provides for the tenure of the judges
Provides for the appointment of the district judges by the Governor in consultation with the High Court
explanation: The Article 233 provides for the appointment of the district judges by the Governor in consultation with the High Court and the Article 234 for the High Court judges.

options: Provides for the removal of a High Court judge by the address of the state legislature
Provides for the removal of a Supreme Court judge
explanation: The Article 217 provides for the removal of a High Court judge by the address of the legislature of the state concerned and the Article 124 for a Supreme Court judge.

options: Provides for the removal of a High Court judge
Provides for the appointment of the judges
Provides for the impeachment of a Supreme Court judge by a two-thirds majority of each house
explanation: The Article 124(4) provides for the impeachment of a Supreme Court judge by an address passed in each house by a two-thirds majority of the total membership and by a majority of the total membership of the house.

options: Empowers the Supreme Court to make the laws and to lay down the procedure
Provides for the appointment of the judges
explanation: The Article 126 empowers the Supreme Court to make the laws and to lay down the procedure and the rules of the same nature as the rules of the Parliament.

options: Deals with the review of the judgments
Empowers the Supreme Court to withdraw and transfer the cases involving the same substantial question of law
Provides for the special leave to appeal
explanation: The Article 139A, inserted in 1987, empowers the Supreme Court to withdraw and transfer the cases involving the same substantial question of law that are pending before several High Courts.

options: Provides for the appointment of the judges of the Supreme Court
explanation: The Article 145 provides for the appointment of the judges of the Supreme Court by the President after consulting the CJI and the senior-most judge and the state Chief Justice.

options: Deals with the salaries and the allowances of the Supreme Court judges
explanation: The Article 146 provides that the salaries, the allowances and the pensions of the Supreme Court judges shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund and shall not be varied to their disadvantage after the appointment.

options: Provides for the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in the criminal cases
explanation: The Article 132 vests the appellate jurisdiction in the Supreme Court in the criminal cases and the Article 134 in the civil cases.

options: Provides for the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in the specified federal disputes
explanation: The Article 131 vests the original jurisdiction in the Supreme Court in the specified federal disputes and the rest is exercised by the High Courts under the Article 226.

options: Empowers the President to refer the matters of the importance or the difficulty to the Supreme Court for its opinion
explanation: The Article 143 empowers the President to refer any matter of importance or difficulty to the Supreme Court for its opinion and the opinion is not binding but is authoritative.

options: Laid down the basic structure doctrine
explanation: The Kesavananda Bharati case of 1973, by a 7-6 majority, laid down the basic structure doctrine and the Minerva Mills case of 1980 harmonised it with the judicial review.

options: Laid down the basic structure doctrine
Held that the fundamental rights could not be amended by the Parliament
explanation: In the Golaknath case the Supreme Court held that the Parliament could not amend the fundamental rights, and it introduced the doctrine of the eclipse.

options: Held that the Article 21 has the procedural and the substantive dimensions
Laid down the basic structure doctrine
explanation: In the Maneka Gandhi case the Supreme Court held that the Article 21 has the procedural and the substantive dimensions and that the procedure must be right, just and fair.

options: Held that the President's Rule is subject to the judicial review
Laid down the basic structure doctrine
explanation: In the S.R. Bommai case the Supreme Court laid down the guidelines for the floor test and held that the proclamation of the President's Rule is subject to the judicial review.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Kesavananda?
options: The Minerva Mills case of 1980 created the NJAC
The Minerva Mills case of 1980 made the right to property fundamental
The Minerva Mills case of 1980 harmonised the basic structure and the judicial review
The Minerva Mills case of 1980 abolished the judicial review
explanation: In the Minerva Mills case of 1980 the Supreme Court held that the harmony and the balance between the parts of the Constitution is a basic feature and that both the judicial review and the basic structure doctrine are complementary.
